name: Panto round glasses

card.summary: Round, slightly flattened eyeglass frames that people wear to add a soft, curved shape to the face and offset angular features.
card.aka: panto frames; round frames; John Lennon style glasses

quick.overview:
Panto glasses are rounded frames, often thin metal or tortoiseshell. People choose them as a styling tool: the curves sit against the straight lines of a square or angular jaw and are said to soften the overall impression of the face.

The effect is visual and lasts while the glasses are worn. No published study has tested whether round frames change how a jaw is perceived, so the idea rests on stylist convention and wearer experience.
quick.how: Wearers pick a round or panto frame in an eyewear shop, matching size to face width and prescription. Thin metal frames give a light look, while thicker acetate gives a bolder, retro one. They are worn the same way as any glasses, with or without a prescription.
quick.risks: Round frames carry no particular health risk. Lens thickness for strong prescriptions and fit across the bridge and temples are the usual practical considerations.

lead: Panto round glasses are eyeglass frames with round or near-round lenses, a style that predates the fashion-accessory era of eyewear and is still widely sold.[1] People in appearance communities use them as a styling choice: the rounded outline is meant to contrast with angular facial features such as a square jaw or strong brow, giving a softer overall look. This is a stylist convention rather than a measured result.

Round lenses are also associated with well-known wearers; the Wikipedia article on glasses notes that the "John Lennon glasses" name comes from his perfectly round metal frames.[1] The same article notes that round frames are the most efficient shape for myopic prescriptions, which keeps lens edges thinner.[1]

angle.text: Panto frames are worn to add curved geometry to the upper face. Wearers and stylists describe this as balancing an angular jawline, and the effect is present only while the glasses are on.

infobox: Round or slightly flattened round lenses

paras: Round and panto shapes are listed among the traditional lens shapes made before glasses became fashion items.[1] Frames range from fine wire rims to thick acetate in tortoiseshell or black.
For strong short-sighted prescriptions, round lenses are described as the most efficient shape, because lens thickness is distributed evenly from the centre.[1]

The stated reason for choosing panto frames is to counter hard angles. Proponents say a round frame next to a square jaw or wide forehead adds contrast and a gentler profile. Others pick them for a retro or intellectual look. Matching frame width to face width is the commonly mentioned fitting point.

timeline.event: Manufacturers begin selling frames as fashion accessories, according to Wikipedia.[1]
